OD1_RETROSPECTIVE_TAXONOMY_VOCABULARY.impact: A enables scalable historical mapping once a complete vocabulary is available; B requires historical taxonomy-version archives that are not currently preserved.
OD1_RETROSPECTIVE_TAXONOMY_VOCABULARY.question: May one frozen later NSE four-tier taxonomy vocabulary be applied retrospectively to point-in-time historical business evidence, with the output explicitly labeled retrospective analytical classification?

OD2_SEMANTIC_SYNONYM_CATALOG.impact: A is conservative but leaves phrases such as HOSPITAL BUSINESS and SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC MODULES unmapped; B can increase coverage but requires explicit mapping review and versioning.
OD2_SEMANTIC_SYNONYM_CATALOG.question: May a reviewed versioned semantic-description to canonical-node synonym catalog be adopted where source text is not an exact canonical label?

OD3_DOMINANT_BUSINESS.impact: A keeps multi-business cases blocked; B may classify some cases but was not previously owner-frozen and therefore cannot be used authoritatively in this canary.
OD3_DOMINANT_BUSINESS.question: What deterministic policy, if any, may convert multi-segment evidence into one economic classification?

OD4_DIVERSIFIED_TREATMENT.impact: No existing methodology family is introduced by this candidate.
OD4_DIVERSIFIED_TREATMENT.question: When no approved dominant-business rule resolves a genuine multi-business company, should it remain classification-blocked for specialized routing or use a separately approved diversified analytical treatment?
